title: agent-hub adapter definition v1
description: Data half of an agent adapter (ARCHITECTURE §3): how to detect, launch, close and present an agent. Read by the desktop app and the hub. Fields that could not be verified for an agent are omitted, never guessed.

gracefulClose.description: Key sequence that lets the agent exit cleanly before its process tree is killed.

permissionKeys.description: Keys the agent's own permission prompt accepts; the permission card sends these.

hooks.description: How the agent runs hook commands and which events agent-hub registers. Informational: for a built-in adapter the hub's installer is the source of truth. Absent for agents that report only through the Agent Integration Protocol.

shell.description: Command form the agent's Windows hook runner needs: cmd (quoted exe path), cmdUnquoted (no quotes; 8.3 path when the path has spaces), powershell (& '<exe>' …), any (shell-neutral: unquoted forward-slash path).

usage.description: Where token usage comes from: none (no data), builtIn (a hub reader for the agent's own files), protocol (Agent Integration Protocol `usage` events). Default: none for user adapters.

screenRules.description: Prompt detection for states the agent has no hook for. A rule's regex is matched against the last `lines` visible lines of the pane's terminal screen, joined with \n. Patterns must stay in the common regex subset (no lookaround, no backreferences).

lines.description: Visible lines, counted from the bottom, the pattern sees. Default 6.

clearOn.description: What ends the matched state: new output or user input. Absent: the state lasts while the rule matches.
